title: Nifty 50 Down 12% From Sept 2024 Peak: Motilal Oswal - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
While the Nifty 50 fell, the Nifty Midcap-150 has remained broadly flat, while the Nifty Smallcap-250 has declined around 1 per cent over the period. | Photo Credit: istock.com

The Nifty 50 has declined 12 per cent from its September 2024 peak, but strong domestic institutional flows, improving earnings prospects and a correction in valuations suggest that the headline market weakness does not fully reflect the underlying fundamentals, according to Motilal Oswal Financial Services.

In its latest India Strategy report, MOFSL said Indian equities have undergone a prolonged phase of consolidation over the past two years amid global, geopolitical and macroeconomic headwinds. However, the brokerage said resilient economic and corporate fundamentals, along with relatively cooler valuations, have improved the risk-reward for Indian equities.

While the Nifty 50 has fallen 12 per cent from its September 2024 peak, the Nifty Midcap-150 has remained broadly flat, while the Nifty Smallcap-250 has declined around 1 per cent over the period.

The market has also witnessed significant sector rotation. Defence, Metals and PSU Banks have been among the key outperformers, gaining 19 per cent, 14 per cent and 10 per cent, respectively. Technology, Consumer, Media and Real Estate have been among the key laggards, declining 18 per cent, 17 per cent, 15 per cent and 12 per cent, respectively.

MOFSL said valuations have corrected significantly from their September 2024 highs. Large-cap and mid-cap valuations have declined by 29 per cent and 27 per cent, respectively, on a 12-month forward P/E basis, while small-cap valuations have corrected by around 4 per cent.

The Nifty 50 is now trading 16 per cent below its long-period average, while mid-caps and small-caps remain 4 per cent and 27 per cent above their respective long-period averages.

The brokerage said the correction in valuations, combined with an improving earnings outlook, has strengthened the risk-reward profile of Indian equities.

Domestic liquidity has continued to provide support to Indian equities despite substantial foreign investor selling.

Over the past 24 months, FII outflows stood at around $56 billion, while DII investments reached approximately $177 billion. Rising monthly SIP contributions have further supported domestic liquidity.

The primary market has also remained active. Between April 2023 and September 2026, ₹10.1 lakh crore was mobilised through IPOs, FPOs, OFS and QIPs, reflecting continued investor participation in equity markets.

MOFSL highlighted several indicators of economic resilience, including 7.8 per cent GDP growth in Q1FY27, robust GST collections, healthy credit growth, strong auto volumes and a recovery in corporate earnings from FY25 lows.

The brokerage estimates around 16 per cent PAT CAGR for both the MOFSL Universe and the Nifty over FY26-28E.

Earnings growth is expected to be stronger across the broader market. MOFSL projects earnings CAGR of 16 per cent for the Nifty 50, 17 per cent for the Nifty Midcap-150 and 27 per cent for the Nifty Smallcap-250 over FY26-28E.

The earnings recovery is also expected to broaden. Around 70 per cent of Nifty-500 companies are expected to deliver more than 15 per cent earnings CAGR over the next two years, compared with 48 per cent in the preceding two years.

Despite the resilient domestic outlook, MOFSL identified higher global bond yields, a renewed rate-hike cycle, geopolitical tensions, energy-price volatility and potential FII outflows as key risks to the market and earnings outlook.

The brokerage expects India’s rate-hike cycle to remain shallow, although a sustained rise in global yields could increase market volatility.

MOFSL said market leadership is likely to remain firmly bottom-up, given the relatively higher earnings growth expected from mid- and small-cap companies.

The brokerage said its preferred Nifty 50 ideas include Bharti Airtel, ICICI Bank, SBI, Titan, Adani Enterprises, M&M, Bharat Electronics, Eternal, Hindalco, Shriram Finance, InterGlobe Aviation and Apollo Hospitals.

Among non-Nifty 50 companies, MOFSL highlighted TVS Motor, BSE, SBI Funds Management, GE Vernova T&D, Lenskart Solutions, Indian Hotels, Meesho, Dixon Technologies, Coforge, Radico Khaitan, Kirloskar Oil Engines, RBL Bank, PhysicsWallah and Inventurus Knowledge Solutions.
